newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open firmer.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open firmer Wednesday, with platinum and palladium making sharp gains overnight as a wildcat strike continued at South Africa's Rustenburg Platinum Holdings, the world's biggest platinum mine.
Dealers said the white metal markets were already tight.
COMEX June gold was called to open $0.80 to $1.00 an ounce higher from Tuesday's close at $344.70 an ounce. Bullion was quoted at $344.75/$345.25 an ounce by dealers.
COMEX July silver was called 1.0 to 2.0 cents an ounce firmer.
June gold traded $345.80 to $344.50 and July silver moved from $4.77 to $4.75 on ACCESS.

But the main focus in overnight dealings was on the heady gains in platinum and palladium as nervousness in an already tight physical market rammed prices higher on news of the South African wildcat strike, dealers said.
The wildcat strike helped to push up prices Tuesday in New York after it began Monday night local time.
Amplats, which operates Rustenburg, said Wednesday that 4,600 employees were still on strike at the Amandelbult section of the mine where there was no morning shift.
Some 15 to 20 percent of production had been affected, Amplats said.
NYMEX July platinum was called $5.00 higher from Tuesday's close of $397.00. On ACCESS, it last traded at $406.00, up $9.00 from Tuesday's settlement.
In London Wednesday, platinum was fixed at $404.50, its highest since August 1996.
NYMEX June palladium was called up $6.00 from Tuesday's close of $174.50. London palladium was fixed at $188.00 today, its highest recorded fixing.
The financial markets Wednesday await U.S. durable goods orders for April, with a rise of 1.3 percent forecast by Wall Street analysts compared to a fall of 2.6 percent in March.
